record.original_question: For n >= 1, let B_n denote the metric completion of the universal metric covering of the configuration space W_n = {(z_1, ..., z_n) in C^n : z_i != z_j for i != j}, equivalently the universal covering of C^n infinitely branching along the hyperplanes z_i = z_j, equipped with the lifted length metric. Is B_n a CAT(0) space for every n?

evidence.quote: Let us define braid space B_n as the universal covering of C_n infinitely branching along the complex hyperplanes z_i = z_j for i != j. We suppose that C_n is equipped with the canonical Euclidean metric, and B_n is equipped with lifted length metric.
In other words, if W_n denotes the complement of complex hyperplanes z_i = z_j in C_n, then the braid space B_n is the completion of the universal metric covering of W_n.
Is it true that B_n is CAT(0) for any n?

artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent (October 2025) gallery of open geometry problems on arXiv, where it is presented as an unresolved question. The closely related problem of whether the braid group itself is CAT(0) is known only up to 6 strands; the metric question for the branched-cover space $B_n$ does not appear to have a published resolution.

status_evidence.title: The 6-strand braid group is CAT(0)
status_evidence.snippet: Demonstrates braid groups with at most 6 strands are CAT(0) via non-crossing partition complexes.
status_evidence.claim: Related CAT(0) questions for braid groups are only resolved for small numbers of strands, suggesting the metric branched-cover version remains open in general.
